root_cause.text: `process_sdp()` in `net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_sip.c` could call the nf_nat_sip `sdp_session` hook with `rtp_addr` left uninitialized because the stack variable was only set when a valid SDP media address was parsed, but the function did not guard against SDP bodies with no usable `m=`/address information.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `bool have_rtp_addr = false`, initializes `rtp_addr` from the session-level `caddr` when available, sets `have_rtp_addr = true` only after copying a valid address, and changes the final hook call from `if (hooks && ct->status & IPS_NAT_MASK)` to `if (hooks && ct->status & IPS_NAT_MASK && have_rtp_addr)`, matching the CVE description that inactive or unrecognized SDP media left `rtp_addr` unassigned yet still passed to `hooks->sdp_session()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce a flag in SDP processing to track whether an RTP address is available.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable named `have_rtp_addr` is declared and initialized to `false` in `process_sdp()`, alongside the existing local variables.
intent_record.how: This adds state to track whether an RTP address has been found or handled during SDP processing, enabling later logic in the function to make decisions based on that condition.

intent_record.intent_summary: Store the parsed SDP RTP address and mark it present when address parsing succeeds.
intent_record.what: In process_sdp(), the single-line if statement handling ct_sip_parse_sdp_addr() was expanded into a braced block, and inside that block two new assignments were added: memcpy(&rtp_addr, &caddr, sizeof(rtp_addr)); and have_rtp_addr = true; while still setting caddr_len = matchlen.
intent_record.how: When an SDP connection/media address is successfully parsed, the code now copies the parsed address into rtp_addr and marks that an RTP address is available. This preserves the discovered RTP address for later use instead of only recording its length, which can affect subsequent RTP-related processing and routing decisions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark RTP address availability when SDP parsing successfully fills `rtp_addr` from either media or connection data.
intent_record.what: The code now sets `have_rtp_addr = true;` in both branches where `rtp_addr` is populated: after copying from `maddr` and after copying from `caddr`. The `else if (caddr_len)` branch was also expanded with braces.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now records that a valid RTP address was obtained whenever it copies either the media address or the connection address into `rtp_addr`. This prevents later logic from treating the address as unavailable after a successful parse and makes the parsed SDP state consistent with the address copy.

intent_record.intent_summary: Require a valid RTP address before updating SDP session state through the NAT SIP hook.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the call to `hooks->sdp_session(...)` was extended by adding `&& have_rtp_addr` to the existing check `hooks && ct->status & IPS_NAT_MASK`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the SDP session update hook is now invoked only when a NAT mapping exists and an RTP address has actually been found, preventing the code from attempting to process or rewrite SDP session information without a valid RTP address.

The reported issue was that `process_sdp()` could call the `sdp_session` hook with `rtp_addr` uninitialized when no usable SDP media/address was parsed. bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present in this function body. The code only calls the NAT hook when NAT is active: `if (hooks && ct->status & IPS_NAT_MASK) ret = hooks->sdp_session(..., &rtp_addr);` and, crucially, `rtp_addr` is initialized on every path that reaches this call. Inside the media loop, it is assigned either from `maddr` (`memcpy(&rtp_addr, &maddr, sizeof(rtp_addr));`) or from the session address `caddr` (`memcpy(&rtp_addr, &caddr, sizeof(rtp_addr));`). If neither a media nor session address can be parsed, the function explicitly aborts earlier with `nf_ct_helper_log(skb, ct, "cannot parse SDP message"); return NF_DROP;`. That means the reported bug condition—calling `sdp_session` with an uninitialized `rtp_addr` due to missing SDP address information—is already prevented here.
